/**
 * Validate Supabase migrations folder sanity.
 *
 * Why: duplicate version prefixes (YYYYMMDDHHMMSS) break Supabase CLI and
 * make it very easy to accidentally push the wrong set of migrations.
 *
 * Run:
 *   pnpm tsx scripts/check-supabase-migrations.ts
 */

import { execSync } from 'node:child_process'
import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs'
import path from 'node:path'

type Problem = {
  kind:
    | 'invalid_name'
    | 'duplicate_version'
    | 'heterogeneous_trigger_row_contract'
    | 'missing_trigger_contract_repair'
  message: string
  files?: string[]
}

type ResolvedTriggerContractException = {
  source: string
  functionName: string
  resolvedBy: string
}

// Applied migrations are immutable. Historical violations stay visible here
// only when a tracked forward migration removes the unsafe function. New
// violations are rejected by both CI and the operator production migration CLI.
const resolvedTriggerContractExceptions: ResolvedTriggerContractException[] = [
  {
    source: 'supabase/migrations/20260721230000_safe_deletion_lifecycle.sql',
    functionName: 'public.reject_inactive_account_write',
    resolvedBy:
      'supabase/migrations/20260722230000_fix_account_write_admission_owner_contract.sql',
  },
]

function gitTrackedMigrations(): string[] {
  const out = execSync('git ls-files supabase/migrations', {
    encoding: 'utf8',
    stdio: ['ignore', 'pipe', 'pipe'],
  })

  return out
    .split(/\r?\n/)
    .map((line) => line.trim())
    .filter(Boolean)
    .filter((file) => file.endsWith('.sql'))
}

function main() {
  const files = gitTrackedMigrations()
  const problems: Problem[] = []

  const versionToFiles = new Map<string, string[]>()

  for (const file of files) {
    const name = path.basename(file)
    const match = /^(\d{14})_/.exec(name)

    if (!match) {
      problems.push({
        kind:<truncated omitted_approx_tokens="150" />TE\s+(?:OR\s+REPLACE\s+)?FUNCTION\s+([a-zA-Z_][\w.]*)[\s\S]*?\$\$[\s\S]*?\$\$\s*;/gi

  for (const file of files) {
    const sql = readFileSync(file, 'utf8')

    for (const match of sql.matchAll(functionPattern)) {
      const functionName = match[1]
      const definition = match[0]
      if (!/\bTG_TABLE_NAME\b/i.test(definition)) continue

      const newFields = new Set(
        Array.from(definition.matchAll(/\bNEW\.([a-zA-Z_][\w]*)/g), (field) =>
          field[1].toLowerCase()
        )
      )
      if (newFields.size <= 1) continue

      const resolvedException = resolvedTriggerContractExceptions.find(
        (exception) =>
          exception.source === file && exception.functionName === functionName
      )

      if (!resolvedException) {
        problems.push({
          kind: 'heterogeneous_trigger_row_contract',
          message:
            `${file}: ${functionName} dispatches on TG_TABLE_NAME while directly reading ` +
            `multiple NEW fields (${Array.from(newFields).sort().join(', ')}). ` +
            'Use explicit row-shape trigger adapters and validate each table/owner contract.',
        })
        continue
      }

      if (!files.includes(resolvedException.resolvedBy)) {
        problems.push({
          kind: 'missing_trigger_contract_repair',
          message:
            `${file}: the historical ${functionName} exception requires tracked forward repair ` +
            resolvedException.resolvedBy,
        })
      }
    }
  }

  if (problems.length > 0) {
    console.error('\n[check-supabase-migrations] FAILED\n')
    for (const problem of problems) {
      console.error(`- ${problem.message}`)
      if (problem.files?.length) {
        for (const file of problem.files) console.error(`  - ${file}`)
      }
    }
    console.error('')
    process.exit(1)
  }

  console.log(`[check-supabase-migrations] OK (${files.length} migrations)`)
}

main()

## Scope and limitations

production replica. It does not prove hosted configuration, OAuth callbacks,
external webhooks, Vercel routing, R2 credentials, or provider behavior.
Preview-branch E2E and controlled production canaries cover those boundaries.
Production writes, migration apply, deployment, alias promotion, and
post-deploy canaries remain separate explicitly authorized operations.

/**
 * Validate Supabase migrations folder sanity.
 *
 * Why: duplicate version prefixes (YYYYMMDDHHMMSS) break Supabase CLI and
 * make it very easy to accidentally push the wrong set of migrations.
 *
 * Run:
 *   pnpm tsx scripts/check-supabase-migrations.ts
 */

import { execSync } from 'node:child_process'
import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs'
import path from 'node:path'

type Problem = {
  kind:
    | 'invalid_name'
    | 'duplicate_version'
    | 'heterogeneous_trigger_row_contract'
    | 'missing_trigger_contract_repair'
  message: string
  files?: string[]
}

type ResolvedTriggerContractException = {
  source: string
  functionName: string
  resolvedBy: string
}

// Applied migrations are immutable. Historical violations stay visible here
// only when a tracked forward migration removes the unsafe function. New
// violations are rejected by both CI and the operator production migration CLI.
const resolvedTriggerContractExceptions: ResolvedTriggerContractException[] = [
  {
    source: 'supabase/migrations/20260721230000_safe_deletion_lifecycle.sql',
    functionName: 'public.reject_inactive_account_write',
    resolvedBy:
      'supabase/migrations/20260722230000_fix_account_write_admission_owner_contract.sql',
  },
]

function gitTrackedMigrations(): string[] {
  const out = execSync('git ls-files supabase/migrations', {
    encoding: 'utf8',
    stdio: ['ignore', 'pipe', 'pipe'],
  })

  return out
    .split(/\r?\n/)
    .map((line) => line.trim())
    .filter(Boolean)
    .filter((file) => file.endsWith('.sql'))
}

function main() {
  const files = gitTrackedMigrations()
  const problems: Problem[] = []

  const versionToFiles = new Map<string, string[]>()

  for (const file of files) {
    const name = path.basename(file)
    const match = /^(\d{14})_/.exec(name)

    if (!match) {
      problems.push({
        kind:<truncated omitted_approx_tokens="150" />TE\s+(?:OR\s+REPLACE\s+)?FUNCTION\s+([a-zA-Z_][\w.]*)[\s\S]*?\$\$[\s\S]*?\$\$\s*;/gi

  for (const file of files) {
    const sql = readFileSync(file, 'utf8')

    for (const match of sql.matchAll(functionPattern)) {
      const functionName = match[1]
      const definition = match[0]
      if (!/\bTG_TABLE_NAME\b/i.test(definition)) continue

      const newFields = new Set(
        Array.from(definition.matchAll(/\bNEW\.([a-zA-Z_][\w]*)/g), (field) =>
          field[1].toLowerCase()
        )
      )
      if (newFields.size <= 1) continue

      const resolvedException = resolvedTriggerContractExceptions.find(
        (exception) =>
          exception.source === file && exception.functionName === functionName
      )

      if (!resolvedException) {
        problems.push({
          kind: 'heterogeneous_trigger_row_contract',
          message:
            `${file}: ${functionName} dispatches on TG_TABLE_NAME while directly reading ` +
            `multiple NEW fields (${Array.from(newFields).sort().join(', ')}). ` +
            'Use explicit row-shape trigger adapters and validate each table/owner contract.',
        })
        continue
      }

      if (!files.includes(resolvedException.resolvedBy)) {
        problems.push({
          kind: 'missing_trigger_contract_repair',
          message:
            `${file}: the historical ${functionName} exception requires tracked forward repair ` +
            resolvedException.resolvedBy,
        })
      }
    }
  }

  if (problems.length > 0) {
    console.error('\n[check-supabase-migrations] FAILED\n')
    for (const problem of problems) {
      console.error(`- ${problem.message}`)
      if (problem.files?.length) {
        for (const file of problem.files) console.error(`  - ${file}`)
      }
    }
    console.error('')
    process.exit(1)
  }

  console.log(`[check-supabase-migrations] OK (${files.length} migrations)`)
}

Jika terdapat beberapa kemungkinan implementasi, pilih solusi yang paling sederhana, aman, maintainable, konsisten dengan codebase, serta tidak menciptakan technical debt atau coupling yang tidak diperlukan.

Implementasikan seluruh requirement pada scope tersebut **secara end-to-end**, bukan hanya sampai UI terlihat selesai atau API berhasil dibuat. Pastikan flow lengkap dari user action/input â†’ validation â†’ frontend/state â†’ API/backend â†’ business logic â†’ persistence/external service â†’ response â†’ final UI/state benar-benar terhubung dan bekerja. Tangani happy path sekaligus kondisi penting seperti invalid input, null/undefined, empty data, malformed payload, network/provider failure, timeout, duplicate action, double-submit, repeated request, partial failure, retry, refresh/reload, async operation, race condition, stale state, authorization failure, dan kondisi lain yang relevan terhadap fitur tersebut. Pastikan validation berada di layer yang tepat, backend tidak mempercayai data penting hanya karena dikirim frontend, permission/ownership diverifikasi secara authoritative, error handling tidak membocorkan informasi sensitif, serta operasi stateful/destructive/berbayar memiliki mekanisme yang aman terhadap retry atau duplicate execution jika diperlukan.

Gunakan dan pertahankan **single source of truth** untuk logic, configuration, model/data mapping, business rule, constants, pricing/cost, capability, atau settings yang memang seharusnya shared. Jangan membuat duplicate implementation hanya agar pekerjaan lebih cepat selesai jika logic yang sama sudah tersedia atau seharusnya diekstrak menjadi reusable/shared layer. Hindari hardcode yang seharusnya configurable, jangan membuat hidden dependency, workaround rapuh, fake fallback, artificial delay, atau logic yang hanya menyembunyikan akar masalah. Jangan melakukan refactor besar terhadap unrelated code dan jangan menambahkan fitur tambahan yang tidak diminta. Jika menemukan masalah di luar scope, catat saja kecuali masalah tersebut benar-benar menjadi blocker terhadap implementasi yang sedang dikerjakan.

Setelah implementasi selesai, lakukan verifikasi nyata terhadap seluruh bagian yang disentuh. Jalankan test yang tersedia dan relevan, lint, type-check, build, unit/integration/e2e test, targeted test, atau validation script lain yang memang digunakan repository. Periksa juga semua caller/dependency yang terdampak agar perubahan tidak menyebabkan regression. Pastikan tidak ada console/runtime error, unhandled rejection, dead code, unused import, duplicate config, debug statement, credential/secret, temporary workaround, atau perubahan file yang tidak diperlukan. Jangan menyatakan fitur sudah bekerja jika hanya berdasarkan code inspection; bedakan dengan jelas antara bagian yang benar-benar diuji secara runtime dan bagian yang hanya diverifikasi secara statis. Jika environment, credential, database, device, atau external service tertentu tidak tersedia, jangan mengarang hasil test dan jelaskan limitation tersebut secara eksplisit.

Sebelum menyelesaikan pekerjaan, lakukan satu final review terhadap seluruh diff dan requirement untuk memastikan tidak ada poin spec yang tertinggal, tidak ada implementasi yang keluar scope, tidak ada behavior existing yang rusak, serta seluruh konfigurasi dan dependency konsisten. Setelah semuanya selesai, berikan laporan yang spesifik berisi: apa yang diimplementasikan, keputusan desain penting, file utama yang berubah, edge case yang ditangani, test/command yang benar-benar dijalankan beserta hasilnya, limitation atau residual risk bila ada, dan bagian yang sengaja tidak dikerjakan karena berada di luar scope. Jika instruksi pekerjaan meminta commit/push, lakukan hanya setelah implementasi dan testing selesai, gunakan commit yang jelas, push ke branch kerja yang ditentukan, dan jangan merge atau deploy kecuali diminta secara eksplisit.

## Scope and limitations

The disposable stack is the required migration/PostgREST contract, not a
production replica. It does not prove hosted configuration, OAuth callbacks,
external webhooks, Vercel routing, R2 credentials, or provider behavior.
Preview-branch E2E and controlled production canaries cover those boundaries.
Production writes, migration apply, deployment, alias promotion, and
post-deploy canaries remain separate explicitly authorized operations.

/**
 * Validate Supabase migrations folder sanity.
 *
 * Why: duplicate version prefixes (YYYYMMDDHHMMSS) break Supabase CLI and
 * make it very easy to accidentally push the wrong set of migrations.
 *
 * Run:
 *   pnpm tsx scripts/check-supabase-migrations.ts
 */

import { execSync } from 'node:child_process'
import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs'
import path from 'node:path'

type Problem = {
  kind:
    | 'invalid_name'
    | 'duplicate_version'
    | 'heterogeneous_trigger_row_contract'
    | 'missing_trigger_contract_repair'
  message: string
  files?: string[]
}

type ResolvedTriggerContractException = {
  source: string
  functionName: string
  resolvedBy: string
}

// Applied migrations are immutable. Historical violations stay visible here
// only when a tracked forward migration removes the unsafe function. New
// violations are rejected by both CI and the operator production migration CLI.
const resolvedTriggerContractExceptions: ResolvedTriggerContractException[] = [
  {
    source: 'supabase/migrations/20260721230000_safe_deletion_lifecycle.sql',
    functionName: 'public.reject_inactive_account_write',
    resolvedBy:
      'supabase/migrations/20260722230000_fix_account_write_admission_owner_contract.sql',
  },
]

function gitTrackedMigrations(): string[] {
  const out = execSync('git ls-files supabase/migrations', {
    encoding: 'utf8',
    stdio: ['ignore', 'pipe', 'pipe'],
  })

  return out
    .split(/\r?\n/)
    .map((line) => line.trim())
    .filter(Boolean)
    .filter((file) => file.endsWith('.sql'))
}

function main() {
  const files = gitTrackedMigrations()
  const problems: Problem[] = []

  const versionToFiles = new Map<string, string[]>()

  for (const file of files) {
    const name = path.basename(file)
    const match = /^(\d{14})_/.exec(name)

    if (!match) {
      problems.push({
        kind:<truncated omitted_approx_tokens="150" />TE\s+(?:OR\s+REPLACE\s+)?FUNCTION\s+([a-zA-Z_][\w.]*)[\s\S]*?\$\$[\s\S]*?\$\$\s*;/gi

  for (const file of files) {
    const sql = readFileSync(file, 'utf8')

    for (const match of sql.matchAll(functionPattern)) {
      const functionName = match[1]
      const definition = match[0]
      if (!/\bTG_TABLE_NAME\b/i.test(definition)) continue

      const newFields = new Set(
        Array.from(definition.matchAll(/\bNEW\.([a-zA-Z_][\w]*)/g), (field) =>
          field[1].toLowerCase()
        )
      )
      if (newFields.size <= 1) continue

      const resolvedException = resolvedTriggerContractExceptions.find(
        (exception) =>
          exception.source === file && exception.functionName === functionName
      )

      if (!resolvedException) {
        problems.push({
          kind: 'heterogeneous_trigger_row_contract',
          message:
            `${file}: ${functionName} dispatches on TG_TABLE_NAME while directly reading ` +
            `multiple NEW fields (${Array.from(newFields).sort().join(', ')}). ` +
            'Use explicit row-shape trigger adapters and validate each table/owner contract.',
        })
        continue
      }

      if (!files.includes(resolvedException.resolvedBy)) {
        problems.push({
          kind: 'missing_trigger_contract_repair',
          message:
            `${file}: the historical ${functionName} exception requires tracked forward repair ` +
            resolvedException.resolvedBy,
        })
      }
    }
  }

  if (problems.length > 0) {
    console.error('\n[check-supabase-migrations] FAILED\n')
    for (const problem of problems) {
      console.error(`- ${problem.message}`)
      if (problem.files?.length) {
        for (const file of problem.files) console.error(`  - ${file}`)
      }
    }
    console.error('')
    process.exit(1)
  }

  console.log(`[check-supabase-migrations] OK (${files.length} migrations)`)
}

main()

/**
 * Validate Supabase migrations folder sanity.
 *
 * Why: duplicate version prefixes (YYYYMMDDHHMMSS) break Supabase CLI and
 * make it very easy to accidentally push the wrong set of migrations.
 *
 * Run:
 *   pnpm tsx scripts/check-supabase-migrations.ts
 */

import { execSync } from 'node:child_process'
import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs'
import path from 'node:path'

type Problem = {
  kind:
    | 'invalid_name'
    | 'duplicate_version'
    | 'heterogeneous_trigger_row_contract'
    | 'missing_trigger_contract_repair'
  message: string
  files?: string[]
}

type ResolvedTriggerContractException = {
  source: string
  functionName: string
  resolvedBy: string
}

// Applied migrations are immutable. Historical violations stay visible here
// only when a tracked forward migration removes the unsafe function. New
// violations are rejected by both CI and the operator production migration CLI.
const resolvedTriggerContractExceptions: ResolvedTriggerContractException[] = [
  {
    source: 'supabase/migrations/20260721230000_safe_deletion_lifecycle.sql',
    functionName: 'public.reject_inactive_account_write',
    resolvedBy:
      'supabase/migrations/20260722230000_fix_account_write_admission_owner_contract.sql',
  },
]

function gitTrackedMigrations(): string[] {
  const out = execSync('git ls-files supabase/migrations', {
    encoding: 'utf8',
    stdio: ['ignore', 'pipe', 'pipe'],
  })

  return out
    .split(/\r?\n/)
    .map((line) => line.trim())
    .filter(Boolean)
    .filter((file) => file.endsWith('.sql'))
}

function main() {
  const files = gitTrackedMigrations()
  const problems: Problem[] = []

  const versionToFiles = new Map<string, string[]>()

  for (const file of files) {
    const name = path.basename(file)
    const match = /^(\d{14})_/.exec(name)

    if (!match) {
      problems.push({
        kind:<truncated omitted_approx_tokens="150" />TE\s+(?:OR\s+REPLACE\s+)?FUNCTION\s+([a-zA-Z_][\w.]*)[\s\S]*?\$\$[\s\S]*?\$\$\s*;/gi

  for (const file of files) {
    const sql = readFileSync(file, 'utf8')

    for (const match of sql.matchAll(functionPattern)) {
      const functionName = match[1]
      const definition = match[0]
      if (!/\bTG_TABLE_NAME\b/i.test(definition)) continue

      const newFields = new Set(
        Array.from(definition.matchAll(/\bNEW\.([a-zA-Z_][\w]*)/g), (field) =>
          field[1].toLowerCase()
        )
      )
      if (newFields.size <= 1) continue

      const resolvedException = resolvedTriggerContractExceptions.find(
        (exception) =>
          exception.source === file && exception.functionName === functionName
      )

      if (!resolvedException) {
        problems.push({
          kind: 'heterogeneous_trigger_row_contract',
          message:
            `${file}: ${functionName} dispatches on TG_TABLE_NAME while directly reading ` +
            `multiple NEW fields (${Array.from(newFields).sort().join(', ')}). ` +
            'Use explicit row-shape trigger adapters and validate each table/owner contract.',
        })
        continue
      }

      if (!files.includes(resolvedException.resolvedBy)) {
        problems.push({
          kind: 'missing_trigger_contract_repair',
          message:
            `${file}: the historical ${functionName} exception requires tracked forward repair ` +
            resolvedException.resolvedBy,
        })
      }
    }
  }

  if (problems.length > 0) {
    console.error('\n[check-supabase-migrations] FAILED\n')
    for (const problem of problems) {
      console.error(`- ${problem.message}`)
      if (problem.files?.length) {
        for (const file of problem.files) console.error(`  - ${file}`)
      }
    }
    console.error('')
    process.exit(1)
  }

  console.log(`[check-supabase-migrations] OK (${files.length} migrations)`)
}

main()

/**
 * Validate Supabase migrations folder sanity.
 *
 * Why: duplicate version prefixes (YYYYMMDDHHMMSS) break Supabase CLI and
 * make it very easy to accidentally push the wrong set of migrations.
 *
 * Run:
 *   pnpm tsx scripts/check-supabase-migrations.ts
 */

import { execSync } from 'node:child_process'
import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs'
import path from 'node:path'

type Problem = {
  kind:
    | 'invalid_name'
    | 'duplicate_version'
    | 'heterogeneous_trigger_row_contract'
    | 'missing_trigger_contract_repair'
  message: string
  files?: string[]
}

type ResolvedTriggerContractException = {
  source: string
  functionName: string
  resolvedBy: string
}

// Applied migrations are immutable. Historical violations stay visible here
// only when a tracked forward migration removes the unsafe function. New
// violations are rejected by both CI and the operator production migration CLI.
const resolvedTriggerContractExceptions: ResolvedTriggerContractException[] = [
  {
    source: 'supabase/migrations/20260721230000_safe_deletion_lifecycle.sql',
    functionName: 'public.reject_inactive_account_write',
    resolvedBy:
      'supabase/migrations/20260722230000_fix_account_write_admission_owner_contract.sql',
  },
]

function gitTrackedMigrations(): string[] {
  const out = execSync('git ls-files supabase/migrations', {
    encoding: 'utf8',
    stdio: ['ignore', 'pipe', 'pipe'],
  })

  return out
    .split(/\r?\n/)
    .map((line) => line.trim())
    .filter(Boolean)
    .filter((file) => file.endsWith('.sql'))
}

function main() {
  const files = gitTrackedMigrations()
  const problems: Problem[] = []

  const versionToFiles = new Map<string, string[]>()

  for (const file of files) {
    const name = path.basename(file)
    const match = /^(\d{14})_/.exec(name)

    if (!match) {
      problems.push({
        kind:<truncated omitted_approx_tokens="150" />TE\s+(?:OR\s+REPLACE\s+)?FUNCTION\s+([a-zA-Z_][\w.]*)[\s\S]*?\$\$[\s\S]*?\$\$\s*;/gi

  for (const file of files) {
    const sql = readFileSync(file, 'utf8')

    for (const match of sql.matchAll(functionPattern)) {
      const functionName = match[1]
      const definition = match[0]
      if (!/\bTG_TABLE_NAME\b/i.test(definition)) continue

      const newFields = new Set(
        Array.from(definition.matchAll(/\bNEW\.([a-zA-Z_][\w]*)/g), (field) =>
          field[1].toLowerCase()
        )
      )
      if (newFields.size <= 1) continue

      const resolvedException = resolvedTriggerContractExceptions.find(
        (exception) =>
          exception.source === file && exception.functionName === functionName
      )

      if (!resolvedException) {
        problems.push({
          kind: 'heterogeneous_trigger_row_contract',
          message:
            `${file}: ${functionName} dispatches on TG_TABLE_NAME while directly reading ` +
            `multiple NEW fields (${Array.from(newFields).sort().join(', ')}). ` +
            'Use explicit row-shape trigger adapters and validate each table/owner contract.',
        })
        continue
      }

      if (!files.includes(resolvedException.resolvedBy)) {
        problems.push({
          kind: 'missing_trigger_contract_repair',
          message:
            `${file}: the historical ${functionName} exception requires tracked forward repair ` +
            resolvedException.resolvedBy,
        })
      }
    }
  }

  if (problems.length > 0) {
    console.error('\n[check-supabase-migrations] FAILED\n')
    for (const problem of problems) {
      console.error(`- ${problem.message}`)
      if (problem.files?.length) {
        for (const file of problem.files) console.error(`  - ${file}`)
      }
    }
    console.error('')
    process.exit(1)
  }

  console.log(`[check-supabase-migrations] OK (${files.length} migrations)`)
}

/**
 * Validate Supabase migrations folder sanity.
 *
 * Why: duplicate version prefixes (YYYYMMDDHHMMSS) break Supabase CLI and
 * make it very easy to accidentally push the wrong set of migrations.
 *
 * Run:
 *   pnpm tsx scripts/check-supabase-migrations.ts
 */

import { execSync } from 'node:child_process'
import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs'
import path from 'node:path'

type Problem = {
  kind:
    | 'invalid_name'
    | 'duplicate_version'
    | 'heterogeneous_trigger_row_contract'
    | 'missing_trigger_contract_repair'
  message: string
  files?: string[]
}

type ResolvedTriggerContractException = {
  source: string
  functionName: string
  resolvedBy: string
}

// Applied migrations are immutable. Historical violations stay visible here
// only when a tracked forward migration removes the unsafe function. New
// violations are rejected by both CI and the operator production migration CLI.
const resolvedTriggerContractExceptions: ResolvedTriggerContractException[] = [
  {
    source: 'supabase/migrations/20260721230000_safe_deletion_lifecycle.sql',
    functionName: 'public.reject_inactive_account_write',
    resolvedBy:
      'supabase/migrations/20260722230000_fix_account_write_admission_owner_contract.sql',
  },
]

function gitTrackedMigrations(): string[] {
  const out = execSync('git ls-files supabase/migrations', {
    encoding: 'utf8',
    stdio: ['ignore', 'pipe', 'pipe'],
  })

  return out
    .split(/\r?\n/)
    .map((line) => line.trim())
    .filter(Boolean)
    .filter((file) => file.endsWith('.sql'))
}

function main() {
  const files = gitTrackedMigrations()
  const problems: Problem[] = []

  const versionToFiles = new Map<string, string[]>()

  for (const file of files) {
    const name = path.basename(file)
    const match = /^(\d{14})_/.exec(name)

    if (!match) {
      problems.push({
        kind:<truncated omitted_approx_tokens="150" />TE\s+(?:OR\s+REPLACE\s+)?FUNCTION\s+([a-zA-Z_][\w.]*)[\s\S]*?\$\$[\s\S]*?\$\$\s*;/gi

  for (const file of files) {
    const sql = readFileSync(file, 'utf8')

    for (const match of sql.matchAll(functionPattern)) {
      const functionName = match[1]
      const definition = match[0]
      if (!/\bTG_TABLE_NAME\b/i.test(definition)) continue

      const newFields = new Set(
        Array.from(definition.matchAll(/\bNEW\.([a-zA-Z_][\w]*)/g), (field) =>
          field[1].toLowerCase()
        )
      )
      if (newFields.size <= 1) continue

      const resolvedException = resolvedTriggerContractExceptions.find(
        (exception) =>
          exception.source === file && exception.functionName === functionName
      )

      if (!resolvedException) {
        problems.push({
          kind: 'heterogeneous_trigger_row_contract',
          message:
            `${file}: ${functionName} dispatches on TG_TABLE_NAME while directly reading ` +
            `multiple NEW fields (${Array.from(newFields).sort().join(', ')}). ` +
            'Use explicit row-shape trigger adapters and validate each table/owner contract.',
        })
        continue
      }

      if (!files.includes(resolvedException.resolvedBy)) {
        problems.push({
          kind: 'missing_trigger_contract_repair',
          message:
            `${file}: the historical ${functionName} exception requires tracked forward repair ` +
            resolvedException.resolvedBy,
        })
      }
    }
  }

  if (problems.length > 0) {
    console.error('\n[check-supabase-migrations] FAILED\n')
    for (const problem of problems) {
      console.error(`- ${problem.message}`)
      if (problem.files?.length) {
        for (const file of problem.files) console.error(`  - ${file}`)
      }
    }
    console.error('')
    process.exit(1)
  }

  console.log(`[check-supabase-migrations] OK (${files.length} migrations)`)
}

/**
 * Validate Supabase migrations folder sanity.
 *
 * Why: duplicate version prefixes (YYYYMMDDHHMMSS) break Supabase CLI and
 * make it very easy to accidentally push the wrong set of migrations.
 *
 * Run:
 *   pnpm tsx scripts/check-supabase-migrations.ts
 */

import { execSync } from 'node:child_process'
import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs'
import path from 'node:path'

type Problem = {
  kind:
    | 'invalid_name'
    | 'duplicate_version'
    | 'heterogeneous_trigger_row_contract'
    | 'missing_trigger_contract_repair'
  message: string
  files?: string[]
}

type ResolvedTriggerContractException = {
  source: string
  functionName: string
  resolvedBy: string
}

// Applied migrations are immutable. Historical violations stay visible here
// only when a tracked forward migration removes the unsafe function. New
// violations are rejected by both CI and the operator production migration CLI.
const resolvedTriggerContractExceptions: ResolvedTriggerContractException[] = [
  {
    source: 'supabase/migrations/20260721230000_safe_deletion_lifecycle.sql',
    functionName: 'public.reject_inactive_account_write',
    resolvedBy:
      'supabase/migrations/20260722230000_fix_account_write_admission_owner_contract.sql',
  },
]

function gitTrackedMigrations(): string[] {
  const out = execSync('git ls-files supabase/migrations', {
    encoding: 'utf8',
    stdio: ['ignore', 'pipe', 'pipe'],
  })

  return out
    .split(/\r?\n/)
    .map((line) => line.trim())
    .filter(Boolean)
    .filter((file) => file.endsWith('.sql'))
}

function main() {
  const files = gitTrackedMigrations()
  const problems: Problem[] = []

  const versionToFiles = new Map<string, string[]>()

  for (const file of files) {
    const name = path.basename(file)
    const match = /^(\d{14})_/.exec(name)

    if (!match) {
      problems.push({
        kind:<truncated omitted_approx_tokens="150" />TE\s+(?:OR\s+REPLACE\s+)?FUNCTION\s+([a-zA-Z_][\w.]*)[\s\S]*?\$\$[\s\S]*?\$\$\s*;/gi

  for (const file of files) {
    const sql = readFileSync(file, 'utf8')

    for (const match of sql.matchAll(functionPattern)) {
      const functionName = match[1]
      const definition = match[0]
      if (!/\bTG_TABLE_NAME\b/i.test(definition)) continue

      const newFields = new Set(
        Array.from(definition.matchAll(/\bNEW\.([a-zA-Z_][\w]*)/g), (field) =>
          field[1].toLowerCase()
        )
      )
      if (newFields.size <= 1) continue

      const resolvedException = resolvedTriggerContractExceptions.find(
        (exception) =>
          exception.source === file && exception.functionName === functionName
      )

      if (!resolvedException) {
        problems.push({
          kind: 'heterogeneous_trigger_row_contract',
          message:
            `${file}: ${functionName} dispatches on TG_TABLE_NAME while directly reading ` +
            `multiple NEW fields (${Array.from(newFields).sort().join(', ')}). ` +
            'Use explicit row-shape trigger adapters and validate each table/owner contract.',
        })
        continue
      }

      if (!files.includes(resolvedException.resolvedBy)) {
        problems.push({
          kind: 'missing_trigger_contract_repair',
          message:
            `${file}: the historical ${functionName} exception requires tracked forward repair ` +
            resolvedException.resolvedBy,
        })
      }
    }
  }

  if (problems.length > 0) {
    console.error('\n[check-supabase-migrations] FAILED\n')
    for (const problem of problems) {
      console.error(`- ${problem.message}`)
      if (problem.files?.length) {
        for (const file of problem.files) console.error(`  - ${file}`)
      }
    }
    console.error('')
    process.exit(1)
  }

  console.log(`[check-supabase-migrations] OK (${files.length} migrations)`)
}

/**
 * Validate Supabase migrations folder sanity.
 *
 * Why: duplicate version prefixes (YYYYMMDDHHMMSS) break Supabase CLI and
 * make it very easy to accidentally push the wrong set of migrations.
 *
 * Run:
 *   pnpm tsx scripts/check-supabase-migrations.ts
 */

import { execSync } from 'node:child_process'
import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs'
import path from 'node:path'

type Problem = {
  kind:
    | 'invalid_name'
    | 'duplicate_version'
    | 'heterogeneous_trigger_row_contract'
    | 'missing_trigger_contract_repair'
  message: string
  files?: string[]
}

type ResolvedTriggerContractException = {
  source: string
  functionName: string
  resolvedBy: string
}

// Applied migrations are immutable. Historical violations stay visible here
// only when a tracked forward migration removes the unsafe function. New
// violations are rejected by both CI and the operator production migration CLI.
const resolvedTriggerContractExceptions: ResolvedTriggerContractException[] = [
  {
    source: 'supabase/migrations/20260721230000_safe_deletion_lifecycle.sql',
    functionName: 'public.reject_inactive_account_write',
    resolvedBy:
      'supabase/migrations/20260722230000_fix_account_write_admission_owner_contract.sql',
  },
]

function gitTrackedMigrations(): string[] {
  const out = execSync('git ls-files supabase/migrations', {
    encoding: 'utf8',
    stdio: ['ignore', 'pipe', 'pipe'],
  })

  return out
    .split(/\r?\n/)
    .map((line) => line.trim())
    .filter(Boolean)
    .filter((file) => file.endsWith('.sql'))
}

function main() {
  const files = gitTrackedMigrations()
  const problems: Problem[] = []

  const versionToFiles = new Map<string, string[]>()

  for (const file of files) {
    const name = path.basename(file)
    const match = /^(\d{14})_/.exec(name)

    if (!match) {
      problems.push({
        kind:<truncated omitted_approx_tokens="150" />TE\s+(?:OR\s+REPLACE\s+)?FUNCTION\s+([a-zA-Z_][\w.]*)[\s\S]*?\$\$[\s\S]*?\$\$\s*;/gi

  for (const file of files) {
    const sql = readFileSync(file, 'utf8')

    for (const match of sql.matchAll(functionPattern)) {
      const functionName = match[1]
      const definition = match[0]
      if (!/\bTG_TABLE_NAME\b/i.test(definition)) continue

      const newFields = new Set(
        Array.from(definition.matchAll(/\bNEW\.([a-zA-Z_][\w]*)/g), (field) =>
          field[1].toLowerCase()
        )
      )
      if (newFields.size <= 1) continue

      const resolvedException = resolvedTriggerContractExceptions.find(
        (exception) =>
          exception.source === file && exception.functionName === functionName
      )

      if (!resolvedException) {
        problems.push({
          kind: 'heterogeneous_trigger_row_contract',
          message:
            `${file}: ${functionName} dispatches on TG_TABLE_NAME while directly reading ` +
            `multiple NEW fields (${Array.from(newFields).sort().join(', ')}). ` +
            'Use explicit row-shape trigger adapters and validate each table/owner contract.',
        })
        continue
      }

      if (!files.includes(resolvedException.resolvedBy)) {
        problems.push({
          kind: 'missing_trigger_contract_repair',
          message:
            `${file}: the historical ${functionName} exception requires tracked forward repair ` +
            resolvedException.resolvedBy,
        })
      }
    }
  }

  if (problems.length > 0) {
    console.error('\n[check-supabase-migrations] FAILED\n')
    for (const problem of problems) {
      console.error(`- ${problem.message}`)
      if (problem.files?.length) {
        for (const file of problem.files) console.error(`  - ${file}`)
      }
    }
    console.error('')
    process.exit(1)
  }

  console.log(`[check-supabase-migrations] OK (${files.length} migrations)`)
}

/**
 * Validate Supabase migrations folder sanity.
 *
 * Why: duplicate version prefixes (YYYYMMDDHHMMSS) break Supabase CLI and
 * make it very easy to accidentally push the wrong set of migrations.
 *
 * Run:
 *   pnpm tsx scripts/check-supabase-migrations.ts
 */

import { execSync } from 'node:child_process'
import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs'
import path from 'node:path'

type Problem = {
  kind:
    | 'invalid_name'
    | 'duplicate_version'
    | 'heterogeneous_trigger_row_contract'
    | 'missing_trigger_contract_repair'
  message: string
  files?: string[]
}

type ResolvedTriggerContractException = {
  source: string
  functionName: string
  resolvedBy: string
}

// Applied migrations are immutable. Historical violations stay visible here
// only when a tracked forward migration removes the unsafe function. New
// violations are rejected by both CI and the operator production migration CLI.
const resolvedTriggerContractExceptions: ResolvedTriggerContractException[] = [
  {
    source: 'supabase/migrations/20260721230000_safe_deletion_lifecycle.sql',
    functionName: 'public.reject_inactive_account_write',
    resolvedBy:
      'supabase/migrations/20260722230000_fix_account_write_admission_owner_contract.sql',
  },
]

function gitTrackedMigrations(): string[] {
  const out = execSync('git ls-files supabase/migrations', {
    encoding: 'utf8',
    stdio: ['ignore', 'pipe', 'pipe'],
  })

  return out
    .split(/\r?\n/)
    .map((line) => line.trim())
    .filter(Boolean)
    .filter((file) => file.endsWith('.sql'))
}

function main() {
  const files = gitTrackedMigrations()
  const problems: Problem[] = []

  const versionToFiles = new Map<string, string[]>()

  for (const file of files) {
    const name = path.basename(file)
    const match = /^(\d{14})_/.exec(name)

    if (!match) {
      problems.push({
        kind:<truncated omitted_approx_tokens="150" />TE\s+(?:OR\s+REPLACE\s+)?FUNCTION\s+([a-zA-Z_][\w.]*)[\s\S]*?\$\$[\s\S]*?\$\$\s*;/gi

  for (const file of files) {
    const sql = readFileSync(file, 'utf8')

    for (const match of sql.matchAll(functionPattern)) {
      const functionName = match[1]
      const definition = match[0]
      if (!/\bTG_TABLE_NAME\b/i.test(definition)) continue

      const newFields = new Set(
        Array.from(definition.matchAll(/\bNEW\.([a-zA-Z_][\w]*)/g), (field) =>
          field[1].toLowerCase()
        )
      )
      if (newFields.size <= 1) continue

      const resolvedException = resolvedTriggerContractExceptions.find(
        (exception) =>
          exception.source === file && exception.functionName === functionName
      )

      if (!resolvedException) {
        problems.push({
          kind: 'heterogeneous_trigger_row_contract',
          message:
            `${file}: ${functionName} dispatches on TG_TABLE_NAME while directly reading ` +
            `multiple NEW fields (${Array.from(newFields).sort().join(', ')}). ` +
            'Use explicit row-shape trigger adapters and validate each table/owner contract.',
        })
        continue
      }

      if (!files.includes(resolvedException.resolvedBy)) {
        problems.push({
          kind: 'missing_trigger_contract_repair',
          message:
            `${file}: the historical ${functionName} exception requires tracked forward repair ` +
            resolvedException.resolvedBy,
        })
      }
    }
  }

  if (problems.length > 0) {
    console.error('\n[check-supabase-migrations] FAILED\n')
    for (const problem of problems) {
      console.error(`- ${problem.message}`)
      if (problem.files?.length) {
        for (const file of problem.files) console.error(`  - ${file}`)
      }
    }
    console.error('')
    process.exit(1)
  }

  console.log(`[check-supabase-migrations] OK (${files.length} migrations)`)
}

/**
 * Validate Supabase migrations folder sanity.
 *
 * Why: duplicate version prefixes (YYYYMMDDHHMMSS) break Supabase CLI and
 * make it very easy to accidentally push the wrong set of migrations.
 *
 * Run:
 *   pnpm tsx scripts/check-supabase-migrations.ts
 */

import { execSync } from 'node:child_process'
import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs'
import path from 'node:path'

type Problem = {
  kind:
    | 'invalid_name'
    | 'duplicate_version'
    | 'heterogeneous_trigger_row_contract'
    | 'missing_trigger_contract_repair'
  message: string
  files?: string[]
}

type ResolvedTriggerContractException = {
  source: string
  functionName: string
  resolvedBy: string
}

// Applied migrations are immutable. Historical violations stay visible here
// only when a tracked forward migration removes the unsafe function. New
// violations are rejected by both CI and the operator production migration CLI.
const resolvedTriggerContractExceptions: ResolvedTriggerContractException[] = [
  {
    source: 'supabase/migrations/20260721230000_safe_deletion_lifecycle.sql',
    functionName: 'public.reject_inactive_account_write',
    resolvedBy:
      'supabase/migrations/20260722230000_fix_account_write_admission_owner_contract.sql',
  },
]

function gitTrackedMigrations(): string[] {
  const out = execSync('git ls-files supabase/migrations', {
    encoding: 'utf8',
    stdio: ['ignore', 'pipe', 'pipe'],
  })

  return out
    .split(/\r?\n/)
    .map((line) => line.trim())
    .filter(Boolean)
    .filter((file) => file.endsWith('.sql'))
}

function main() {
  const files = gitTrackedMigrations()
  const problems: Problem[] = []

  const versionToFiles = new Map<string, string[]>()

  for (const file of files) {
    const name = path.basename(file)
    const match = /^(\d{14})_/.exec(name)

    if (!match) {
      problems.push({
        kind:<truncated omitted_approx_tokens="150" />TE\s+(?:OR\s+REPLACE\s+)?FUNCTION\s+([a-zA-Z_][\w.]*)[\s\S]*?\$\$[\s\S]*?\$\$\s*;/gi

  for (const file of files) {
    const sql = readFileSync(file, 'utf8')

    for (const match of sql.matchAll(functionPattern)) {
      const functionName = match[1]
      const definition = match[0]
      if (!/\bTG_TABLE_NAME\b/i.test(definition)) continue

      const newFields = new Set(
        Array.from(definition.matchAll(/\bNEW\.([a-zA-Z_][\w]*)/g), (field) =>
          field[1].toLowerCase()
        )
      )
      if (newFields.size <= 1) continue

      const resolvedException = resolvedTriggerContractExceptions.find(
        (exception) =>
          exception.source === file && exception.functionName === functionName
      )

      if (!resolvedException) {
        problems.push({
          kind: 'heterogeneous_trigger_row_contract',
          message:
            `${file}: ${functionName} dispatches on TG_TABLE_NAME while directly reading ` +
            `multiple NEW fields (${Array.from(newFields).sort().join(', ')}). ` +
            'Use explicit row-shape trigger adapters and validate each table/owner contract.',
        })
        continue
      }

      if (!files.includes(resolvedException.resolvedBy)) {
        problems.push({
          kind: 'missing_trigger_contract_repair',
          message:
            `${file}: the historical ${functionName} exception requires tracked forward repair ` +
            resolvedException.resolvedBy,
        })
      }
    }
  }

  if (problems.length > 0) {
    console.error('\n[check-supabase-migrations] FAILED\n')
    for (const problem of problems) {
      console.error(`- ${problem.message}`)
      if (problem.files?.length) {
        for (const file of problem.files) console.error(`  - ${file}`)
      }
    }
    console.error('')
    process.exit(1)
  }

  console.log(`[check-supabase-migrations] OK (${files.length} migrations)`)
}

/**
 * Validate Supabase migrations folder sanity.
 *
 * Why: duplicate version prefixes (YYYYMMDDHHMMSS) break Supabase CLI and
 * make it very easy to accidentally push the wrong set of migrations.
 *
 * Run:
 *   pnpm tsx scripts/check-supabase-migrations.ts
 */

import { execSync } from 'node:child_process'
import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs'
import path from 'node:path'

type Problem = {
  kind:
    | 'invalid_name'
    | 'duplicate_version'
    | 'heterogeneous_trigger_row_contract'
    | 'missing_trigger_contract_repair'
  message: string
  files?: string[]
}

type ResolvedTriggerContractException = {
  source: string
  functionName: string
  resolvedBy: string
}

// Applied migrations are immutable. Historical violations stay visible here
// only when a tracked forward migration removes the unsafe function. New
// violations are rejected by both CI and the operator production migration CLI.
const resolvedTriggerContractExceptions: ResolvedTriggerContractException[] = [
  {
    source: 'supabase/migrations/20260721230000_safe_deletion_lifecycle.sql',
    functionName: 'public.reject_inactive_account_write',
    resolvedBy:
      'supabase/migrations/20260722230000_fix_account_write_admission_owner_contract.sql',
  },
]

function gitTrackedMigrations(): string[] {
  const out = execSync('git ls-files supabase/migrations', {
    encoding: 'utf8',
    stdio: ['ignore', 'pipe', 'pipe'],
  })

  return out
    .split(/\r?\n/)
    .map((line) => line.trim())
    .filter(Boolean)
    .filter((file) => file.endsWith('.sql'))
}

function main() {
  const files = gitTrackedMigrations()
  const problems: Problem[] = []

  const versionToFiles = new Map<string, string[]>()

  for (const file of files) {
    const name = path.basename(file)
    const match = /^(\d{14})_/.exec(name)

    if (!match) {
      problems.push({
        kind:<truncated omitted_approx_tokens="150" />TE\s+(?:OR\s+REPLACE\s+)?FUNCTION\s+([a-zA-Z_][\w.]*)[\s\S]*?\$\$[\s\S]*?\$\$\s*;/gi

  for (const file of files) {
    const sql = readFileSync(file, 'utf8')

    for (const match of sql.matchAll(functionPattern)) {
      const functionName = match[1]
      const definition = match[0]
      if (!/\bTG_TABLE_NAME\b/i.test(definition)) continue

      const newFields = new Set(
        Array.from(definition.matchAll(/\bNEW\.([a-zA-Z_][\w]*)/g), (field) =>
          field[1].toLowerCase()
        )
      )
      if (newFields.size <= 1) continue

      const resolvedException = resolvedTriggerContractExceptions.find(
        (exception) =>
          exception.source === file && exception.functionName === functionName
      )

      if (!resolvedException) {
        problems.push({
          kind: 'heterogeneous_trigger_row_contract',
          message:
            `${file}: ${functionName} dispatches on TG_TABLE_NAME while directly reading ` +
            `multiple NEW fields (${Array.from(newFields).sort().join(', ')}). ` +
            'Use explicit row-shape trigger adapters and validate each table/owner contract.',
        })
        continue
      }

      if (!files.includes(resolvedException.resolvedBy)) {
        problems.push({
          kind: 'missing_trigger_contract_repair',
          message:
            `${file}: the historical ${functionName} exception requires tracked forward repair ` +
            resolvedException.resolvedBy,
        })
      }
    }
  }

  if (problems.length > 0) {
    console.error('\n[check-supabase-migrations] FAILED\n')
    for (const problem of problems) {
      console.error(`- ${problem.message}`)
      if (problem.files?.length) {
        for (const file of problem.files) console.error(`  - ${file}`)
      }
    }
    console.error('')
    process.exit(1)
  }

  console.log(`[check-supabase-migrations] OK (${files.length} migrations)`)
}

Identifikasi dengan jelas apa yang termasuk scope dan apa yang tidak termasuk scope. Jangan langsung coding berdasarkan asumsi; cocokkan requirement dengan implementasi aktual di repository dan gunakan existing pattern sebagai acuan utama selama tidak bertentangan dengan spec. Jika terdapat beberapa kemungkinan implementasi, pilih solusi yang paling sederhana, aman, maintainable, konsisten dengan codebase, serta tidak menciptakan technical debt atau coupling yang tidak diperlukan.

Implementasikan seluruh requirement pada scope tersebut **secara end-to-end**, bukan hanya sampai UI terlihat selesai atau API berhasil dibuat. Pastikan flow lengkap dari user action/input â†’ validation â†’ frontend/state â†’ API/backend â†’ business logic â†’ persistence/external service â†’ response â†’ final UI/state benar-benar terhubung dan bekerja. Jangan membuat duplicate implementation hanya agar pekerjaan lebih cepat selesai jika logic yang sama sudah tersedia atau seharusnya diekstrak menjadi reusable/shared layer. Hindari hardcode yang seharusnya configurable, jangan membuat hidden dependency, workaround rapuh, fake fallback, artificial delay, atau logic yang hanya menyembunyikan akar masalah. Jangan melakukan refactor besar terhadap unrelated code dan jangan menambahkan fitur tambahan yang tidak diminta. Jika menemukan masalah di luar scope, catat saja kecuali masalah tersebut benar-benar menjadi blocker terhadap implementasi yang sedang dikerjakan.

Setelah semuanya selesai, berikan laporan yang spesifik berisi: apa yang diimplementasikan, keputusan desain penting, file utama yang berubah, edge case yang ditangani, test/command yang benar-benar dijalankan beserta hasilnya, limitation atau residual risk bila ada, dan bagian yang sengaja tidak dikerjakan karena berada di luar scope. /**
 * Validate Supabase migrations folder sanity.
 *
 * Why: duplicate version prefixes (YYYYMMDDHHMMSS) break Supabase CLI and
 * make it very easy to accidentally push the wrong set of migrations.
 *
 * Run:
 *   pnpm tsx scripts/check-supabase-migrations.ts
 */

import { execSync } from 'node:child_process'
import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs'
import path from 'node:path'

type Problem = {
  kind:
    | 'invalid_name'
    | 'duplicate_version'
    | 'heterogeneous_trigger_row_contract'
    | 'missing_trigger_contract_repair'
  message: string
  files?: string[]
}

type ResolvedTriggerContractException = {
  source: string
  functionName: string
  resolvedBy: string
}

// Applied migrations are immutable. Historical violations stay visible here
// only when a tracked forward migration removes the unsafe function. New
// violations are rejected by both CI and the operator production migration CLI.
const resolvedTriggerContractExceptions: ResolvedTriggerContractException[] = [
  {
    source: 'supabase/migrations/20260721230000_safe_deletion_lifecycle.sql',
    functionName: 'public.reject_inactive_account_write',
    resolvedBy:
      'supabase/migrations/20260722230000_fix_account_write_admission_owner_contract.sql',
  },
]

function gitTrackedMigrations(): string[] {
  const out = execSync('git ls-files supabase/migrations', {
    encoding: 'utf8',
    stdio: ['ignore', 'pipe', 'pipe'],
  })

  return out
    .split(/\r?\n/)
    .map((line) => line.trim())
    .filter(Boolean)
    .filter((file) => file.endsWith('.sql'))
}

function main() {
  const files = gitTrackedMigrations()
  const problems: Problem[] = []

  const versionToFiles = new Map<string, string[]>()

  for (const file of files) {
    const name = path.basename(file)
    const match = /^(\d{14})_/.exec(name)

    if (!match) {
      problems.push({
        kind:<truncated omitted_approx_tokens="150" />TE\s+(?:OR\s+REPLACE\s+)?FUNCTION\s+([a-zA-Z_][\w.]*)[\s\S]*?\$\$[\s\S]*?\$\$\s*;/gi

  for (const file of files) {
    const sql = readFileSync(file, 'utf8')

    for (const match of sql.matchAll(functionPattern)) {
      const functionName = match[1]
      const definition = match[0]
      if (!/\bTG_TABLE_NAME\b/i.test(definition)) continue

      const newFields = new Set(
        Array.from(definition.matchAll(/\bNEW\.([a-zA-Z_][\w]*)/g), (field) =>
          field[1].toLowerCase()
        )
      )
      if (newFields.size <= 1) continue

      const resolvedException = resolvedTriggerContractExceptions.find(
        (exception) =>
          exception.source === file && exception.functionName === functionName
      )

      if (!resolvedException) {
        problems.push({
          kind: 'heterogeneous_trigger_row_contract',
          message:
            `${file}: ${functionName} dispatches on TG_TABLE_NAME while directly reading ` +
            `multiple NEW fields (${Array.from(newFields).sort().join(', ')}). ` +
            'Use explicit row-shape trigger adapters and validate each table/owner contract.',
        })
        continue
      }

      if (!files.includes(resolvedException.resolvedBy)) {
        problems.push({
          kind: 'missing_trigger_contract_repair',
          message:
            `${file}: the historical ${functionName} exception requires tracked forward repair ` +
            resolvedException.resolvedBy,
        })
      }
    }
  }

  if (problems.length > 0) {
    console.error('\n[check-supabase-migrations] FAILED\n')
    for (const problem of problems) {
      console.error(`- ${problem.message}`)
      if (problem.files?.length) {
        for (const file of problem.files) console.error(`  - ${file}`)
      }
    }
    console.error('')
    process.exit(1)
  }

  console.log(`[check-supabase-migrations] OK (${files.length} migrations)`)
}

main()

/**
 * Validate Supabase migrations folder sanity.
 *
 * Why: duplicate version prefixes (YYYYMMDDHHMMSS) break Supabase CLI and
 * make it very easy to accidentally push the wrong set of migrations.
 *
 * Run:
 *   pnpm tsx scripts/check-supabase-migrations.ts
 */

import { execSync } from 'node:child_process'
import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs'
import path from 'node:path'

type Problem = {
  kind:
    | 'invalid_name'
    | 'duplicate_version'
    | 'heterogeneous_trigger_row_contract'
    | 'missing_trigger_contract_repair'
  message: string
  files?: string[]
}

type ResolvedTriggerContractException = {
  source: string
  functionName: string
  resolvedBy: string
}

// Applied migrations are immutable. Historical violations stay visible here
// only when a tracked forward migration removes the unsafe function. New
// violations are rejected by both CI and the operator production migration CLI.
const resolvedTriggerContractExceptions: ResolvedTriggerContractException[] = [
  {
    source: 'supabase/migrations/20260721230000_safe_deletion_lifecycle.sql',
    functionName: 'public.reject_inactive_account_write',
    resolvedBy:
      'supabase/migrations/20260722230000_fix_account_write_admission_owner_contract.sql',
  },
]

function gitTrackedMigrations(): string[] {
  const out = execSync('git ls-files supabase/migrations', {
    encoding: 'utf8',
    stdio: ['ignore', 'pipe', 'pipe'],
  })

  return out
    .split(/\r?\n/)
    .map((line) => line.trim())
    .filter(Boolean)
    .filter((file) => file.endsWith('.sql'))
}

function main() {
  const files = gitTrackedMigrations()
  const problems: Problem[] = []

  const versionToFiles = new Map<string, string[]>()

  for (const file of files) {
    const name = path.basename(file)
    const match = /^(\d{14})_/.exec(name)

    if (!match) {
      problems.push({
        kind:<truncated omitted_approx_tokens="150" />TE\s+(?:OR\s+REPLACE\s+)?FUNCTION\s+([a-zA-Z_][\w.]*)[\s\S]*?\$\$[\s\S]*?\$\$\s*;/gi

  for (const file of files) {
    const sql = readFileSync(file, 'utf8')

    for (const match of sql.matchAll(functionPattern)) {
      const functionName = match[1]
      const definition = match[0]
      if (!/\bTG_TABLE_NAME\b/i.test(definition)) continue

      const newFields = new Set(
        Array.from(definition.matchAll(/\bNEW\.([a-zA-Z_][\w]*)/g), (field) =>
          field[1].toLowerCase()
        )
      )
      if (newFields.size <= 1) continue

      const resolvedException = resolvedTriggerContractExceptions.find(
        (exception) =>
          exception.source === file && exception.functionName === functionName
      )

      if (!resolvedException) {
        problems.push({
          kind: 'heterogeneous_trigger_row_contract',
          message:
            `${file}: ${functionName} dispatches on TG_TABLE_NAME while directly reading ` +
            `multiple NEW fields (${Array.from(newFields).sort().join(', ')}). ` +
            'Use explicit row-shape trigger adapters and validate each table/owner contract.',
        })
        continue
      }

      if (!files.includes(resolvedException.resolvedBy)) {
        problems.push({
          kind: 'missing_trigger_contract_repair',
          message:
            `${file}: the historical ${functionName} exception requires tracked forward repair ` +
            resolvedException.resolvedBy,
        })
      }
    }
  }

  if (problems.length > 0) {
    console.error('\n[check-supabase-migrations] FAILED\n')
    for (const problem of problems) {
      console.error(`- ${problem.message}`)
      if (problem.files?.length) {
        for (const file of problem.files) console.error(`  - ${file}`)
      }
    }
    console.error('')
    process.exit(1)
  }

  console.log(`[check-supabase-migrations] OK (${files.length} migrations)`)
}

/**
 * Validate Supabase migrations folder sanity.
 *
 * Why: duplicate version prefixes (YYYYMMDDHHMMSS) break Supabase CLI and
 * make it very easy to accidentally push the wrong set of migrations.
 *
 * Run:
 *   pnpm tsx scripts/check-supabase-migrations.ts
 */

import { execSync } from 'node:child_process'
import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs'
import path from 'node:path'

type Problem = {
  kind:
    | 'invalid_name'
    | 'duplicate_version'
    | 'heterogeneous_trigger_row_contract'
    | 'missing_trigger_contract_repair'
  message: string
  files?: string[]
}

type ResolvedTriggerContractException = {
  source: string
  functionName: string
  resolvedBy: string
}

// Applied migrations are immutable. Historical violations stay visible here
// only when a tracked forward migration removes the unsafe function. New
// violations are rejected by both CI and the operator production migration CLI.
const resolvedTriggerContractExceptions: ResolvedTriggerContractException[] = [
  {
    source: 'supabase/migrations/20260721230000_safe_deletion_lifecycle.sql',
    functionName: 'public.reject_inactive_account_write',
    resolvedBy:
      'supabase/migrations/20260722230000_fix_account_write_admission_owner_contract.sql',
  },
]

function gitTrackedMigrations(): string[] {
  const out = execSync('git ls-files supabase/migrations', {
    encoding: 'utf8',
    stdio: ['ignore', 'pipe', 'pipe'],
  })

  return out
    .split(/\r?\n/)
    .map((line) => line.trim())
    .filter(Boolean)
    .filter((file) => file.endsWith('.sql'))
}

function main() {
  const files = gitTrackedMigrations()
  const problems: Problem[] = []

  const versionToFiles = new Map<string, string[]>()

  for (const file of files) {
    const name = path.basename(file)
    const match = /^(\d{14})_/.exec(name)

    if (!match) {
      problems.push({
        kind:<truncated omitted_approx_tokens="150" />TE\s+(?:OR\s+REPLACE\s+)?FUNCTION\s+([a-zA-Z_][\w.]*)[\s\S]*?\$\$[\s\S]*?\$\$\s*;/gi

  for (const file of files) {
    const sql = readFileSync(file, 'utf8')

    for (const match of sql.matchAll(functionPattern)) {
      const functionName = match[1]
      const definition = match[0]
      if (!/\bTG_TABLE_NAME\b/i.test(definition)) continue

      const newFields = new Set(
        Array.from(definition.matchAll(/\bNEW\.([a-zA-Z_][\w]*)/g), (field) =>
          field[1].toLowerCase()
        )
      )
      if (newFields.size <= 1) continue

      const resolvedException = resolvedTriggerContractExceptions.find(
        (exception) =>
          exception.source === file && exception.functionName === functionName
      )

      if (!resolvedException) {
        problems.push({
          kind: 'heterogeneous_trigger_row_contract',
          message:
            `${file}: ${functionName} dispatches on TG_TABLE_NAME while directly reading ` +
            `multiple NEW fields (${Array.from(newFields).sort().join(', ')}). ` +
            'Use explicit row-shape trigger adapters and validate each table/owner contract.',
        })
        continue
      }

      if (!files.includes(resolvedException.resolvedBy)) {
        problems.push({
          kind: 'missing_trigger_contract_repair',
          message:
            `${file}: the historical ${functionName} exception requires tracked forward repair ` +
            resolvedException.resolvedBy,
        })
      }
    }
  }

  if (problems.length > 0) {
    console.error('\n[check-supabase-migrations] FAILED\n')
    for (const problem of problems) {
      console.error(`- ${problem.message}`)
      if (problem.files?.length) {
        for (const file of problem.files) console.error(`  - ${file}`)
      }
    }
    console.error('')
    process.exit(1)
  }

  console.log(`[check-supabase-migrations] OK (${files.length} migrations)`)
}

main()

/**
 * Validate Supabase migrations folder sanity.
 *
 * Why: duplicate version prefixes (YYYYMMDDHHMMSS) break Supabase CLI and
 * make it very easy to accidentally push the wrong set of migrations.
 *
 * Run:
 *   pnpm tsx scripts/check-supabase-migrations.ts
 */

import { execSync } from 'node:child_process'
import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs'
import path from 'node:path'

type Problem = {
  kind:
    | 'invalid_name'
    | 'duplicate_version'
    | 'heterogeneous_trigger_row_contract'
    | 'missing_trigger_contract_repair'
  message: string
  files?: string[]
}

type ResolvedTriggerContractException = {
  source: string
  functionName: string
  resolvedBy: string
}

// Applied migrations are immutable. Historical violations stay visible here
// only when a tracked forward migration removes the unsafe function. New
// violations are rejected by both CI and the operator production migration CLI.
const resolvedTriggerContractExceptions: ResolvedTriggerContractException[] = [
  {
    source: 'supabase/migrations/20260721230000_safe_deletion_lifecycle.sql',
    functionName: 'public.reject_inactive_account_write',
    resolvedBy:
      'supabase/migrations/20260722230000_fix_account_write_admission_owner_contract.sql',
  },
]

function gitTrackedMigrations(): string[] {
  const out = execSync('git ls-files supabase/migrations', {
    encoding: 'utf8',
    stdio: ['ignore', 'pipe', 'pipe'],
  })

  return out
    .split(/\r?\n/)
    .map((line) => line.trim())
    .filter(Boolean)
    .filter((file) => file.endsWith('.sql'))
}

    const sql = readFileSync(file, 'utf8')

    for (const match of sql.matchAll(functionPattern)) {
      const functionName = match[1]
      const definition = match[0]
      if (!/\bTG_TABLE_NAME\b/i.test(definition)) continue

      const newFields = new Set(
        Array.from(definition.matchAll(/\bNEW\.([a-zA-Z_][\w]*)/g), (field) =>
          field[1].toLowerCase()
        )
      )
      if (newFields.size <= 1) continue

      const resolvedException = resolvedTriggerContractExceptions.find(
        (exception) =>
          exception.source === file && exception.functionName === functionName
      )

      if (!resolvedException) {
        problems.push({
          kind: 'heterogeneous_trigger_row_contract',
          message:
            `${file}: ${functionName} dispatches on TG_TABLE_NAME while directly reading ` +
            `multiple NEW fields (${Array.from(newFields).sort().join(', ')}). ` +
            'Use explicit row-shape trigger adapters and validate each table/owner contract.',
        })
        continue
      }

      if (!files.includes(resolvedException.resolvedBy)) {
        problems.push({
          kind: 'missing_trigger_contract_repair',
          message:
            `${file}: the historical ${functionName} exception requires tracked forward repair ` +
            resolvedException.resolvedBy,
        })
      }
    }
  }

  if (problems.length > 0) {
    console.error('\n[check-supabase-migrations] FAILED\n')
    for (const problem of problems) {
      console.error(`- ${problem.message}`)
      if (problem.files?.length) {
        for (const file of problem.files) console.error(`  - ${file}`)
      }
    }
    console.error('')
    process.exit(1)
  }

  console.log(`[check-supabase-migrations] OK (${files.length} migrations)`)
}

main()

  message: string
  files?: string[]
}

type ResolvedTriggerContractException = {
  source: string
  functionName: string
  resolvedBy: string
}

// Applied migrations are immutable. Historical violations stay visible here
// only when a tracked forward migration removes the unsafe function. New
// violations are rejected by both CI and the operator production migration CLI.
const resolvedTriggerContractExceptions: ResolvedTriggerContractException[] = [
  {
    source: 'supabase/migrations/20260721230000_safe_deletion_lifecycle.sql',
    functionName: 'public.reject_inactive_account_write',
    resolvedBy:
      'supabase/migrations/20260722230000_fix_account_write_admission_owner_contract.sql',
  },
]

function gitTrackedMigrations(): string[] {
  const out = execSync('git ls-files supabase/migrations', {
    encoding: 'utf8',
    stdio: ['ignore', 'pipe', 'pipe'],
  })

  return out
    .split(/\r?\n/)
    .map((line) => line.trim())
    .filter(Boolean)
    .filter((file) => file.endsWith('.sql'))
}

function main() {
  const files = gitTrackedMigrations()
  const problems: Problem[] = []

  const versionToFiles = new Map<string, string[]>()

  for (const file of files) {
    const name = path.basename(file)
    const match = /^(\d{14})_/.exec(name)

    if (!match) {
      problems.push({
        kind:<truncated omitted_approx_tokens="150" />TE\s+(?:OR\s+REPLACE\s+)?FUNCTION\s+([a-zA-Z_][\w.]*)[\s\S]*?\$\$[\s\S]*?\$\$\s*;/gi

  for (const file of files) {
    const sql = readFileSync(file, 'utf8')

    for (const match of sql.matchAll(functionPattern)) {
      const functionName = match[1]
      const definition = match[0]
      if (!/\bTG_TABLE_NAME\b/i.test(definition)) continue

      const newFields = new Set(
        Array.from(definition.matchAll(/\bNEW\.([a-zA-Z_][\w]*)/g), (field) =>
          field[1].toLowerCase()
        )
      )
      if (newFields.size <= 1) continue

      const resolvedException = resolvedTriggerContractExceptions.find(
        (exception) =>
          exception.source === file && exception.functionName === functionName
      )

      if (!resolvedException) {
        problems.push({
          kind: 'heterogeneous_trigger_row_contract',
          message:
            `${file}: ${functionName} dispatches on TG_TABLE_NAME while directly reading ` +
            `multiple NEW fields (${Array.from(newFields).sort().join(', ')}). ` +
            'Use explicit row-shape trigger adapters and validate each table/owner contract.',
        })
        continue
      }

      if (!files.includes(resolvedException.resolvedBy)) {
        problems.push({
          kind: 'missing_trigger_contract_repair',
          message:
            `${file}: the historical ${functionName} exception requires tracked forward repair ` +
            resolvedException.resolvedBy,
        })
      }
    }
  }

  if (problems.length > 0) {
    console.error('\n[check-supabase-migrations] FAILED\n')
    for (const problem of problems) {
      console.error(`- ${problem.message}`)
      if (problem.files?.length) {
        for (const file of problem.files) console.error(`  - ${file}`)
      }
    }
    console.error('')
    process.exit(1)
  }

  console.log(`[check-supabase-migrations] OK (${files.length} migrations)`)
}

/**
 * Validate Supabase migrations folder sanity.
 *
 * Why: duplicate version prefixes (YYYYMMDDHHMMSS) break Supabase CLI and
 * make it very easy to accidentally push the wrong set of migrations.
 *
 * Run:
 *   pnpm tsx scripts/check-supabase-migrations.ts
 */

import { execSync } from 'node:child_process'
import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs'
import path from 'node:path'

type Problem = {
  kind:
    | 'invalid_name'
    | 'duplicate_version'
    | 'heterogeneous_trigger_row_contract'
    | 'missing_trigger_contract_repair'
  message: string
  files?: string[]
}

type ResolvedTriggerContractException = {
  source: string
  functionName: string
  resolvedBy: string
}

// Applied migrations are immutable. Historical violations stay visible here
// only when a tracked forward migration removes the unsafe function. New
// violations are rejected by both CI and the operator production migration CLI.
const resolvedTriggerContractExceptions: ResolvedTriggerContractException[] = [
  {
    source: 'supabase/migrations/20260721230000_safe_deletion_lifecycle.sql',
    functionName: 'public.reject_inactive_account_write',
    resolvedBy:
      'supabase/migrations/20260722230000_fix_account_write_admission_owner_contract.sql',
  },
]

function gitTrackedMigrations(): string[] {
  const out = execSync('git ls-files supabase/migrations', {
    encoding: 'utf8',
    stdio: ['ignore', 'pipe', 'pipe'],
  })

  return out
    .split(/\r?\n/)
    .map((line) => line.trim())
    .filter(Boolean)
    .filter((file) => file.endsWith('.sql'))
}

function main() {
  const files = gitTrackedMigrations()
  const problems: Problem[] = []

  const versionToFiles = new Map<string, string[]>()

  for (const file of files) {
    const name = path.basename(file)
    const match = /^(\d{14})_/.exec(name)

    if (!match) {
      problems.push({
        kind:<truncated omitted_approx_tokens="150" />TE\s+(?:OR\s+REPLACE\s+)?FUNCTION\s+([a-zA-Z_][\w.]*)[\s\S]*?\$\$[\s\S]*?\$\$\s*;/gi

  for (const file of files) {
    const sql = readFileSync(file, 'utf8')

    for (const match of sql.matchAll(functionPattern)) {
      const functionName = match[1]
      const definition = match[0]
      if (!/\bTG_TABLE_NAME\b/i.test(definition)) continue

      const newFields = new Set(
        Array.from(definition.matchAll(/\bNEW\.([a-zA-Z_][\w]*)/g), (field) =>
          field[1].toLowerCase()
        )
      )
      if (newFields.size <= 1) continue

      const resolvedException = resolvedTriggerContractExceptions.find(
        (exception) =>
          exception.source === file && exception.functionName === functionName
      )

      if (!resolvedException) {
        problems.push({
          kind: 'heterogeneous_trigger_row_contract',
          message:
            `${file}: ${functionName} dispatches on TG_TABLE_NAME while directly reading ` +
            `multiple NEW fields (${Array.from(newFields).sort().join(', ')}). ` +
            'Use explicit row-shape trigger adapters and validate each table/owner contract.',
        })
        continue
      }

      if (!files.includes(resolvedException.resolvedBy)) {
        problems.push({
          kind: 'missing_trigger_contract_repair',
          message:
            `${file}: the historical ${functionName} exception requires tracked forward repair ` +
            resolvedException.resolvedBy,
        })
      }
    }
  }

  if (problems.length > 0) {
    console.error('\n[check-supabase-migrations] FAILED\n')
    for (const problem of problems) {
      console.error(`- ${problem.message}`)
      if (problem.files?.length) {
        for (const file of problem.files) console.error(`  - ${file}`)
      }
    }
    console.error('')
    process.exit(1)
  }

  console.log(`[check-supabase-migrations] OK (${files.length} migrations)`)
}

main()

# notifications. Under shared Docker I/O pressure, the existing PostgREST
# connection pool can remain wedged even though PostgreSQL is healthy. Restart

# shared Docker disk is under CI pressure. Keep each request short, but give
# PostgREST a bounded nine-minute recovery window.

Jangan membuat duplicate implementation hanya agar pekerjaan lebih cepat selesai jika logic yang sama sudah tersedia atau seharusnya diekstrak menjadi reusable/shared layer. Hindari hardcode yang seharusnya configurable, jangan membuat hidden dependency, workaround rapuh, fake fallback, artificial delay, atau logic yang hanya menyembunyikan akar masalah. Jangan melakukan refactor besar terhadap unrelated code dan jangan menambahkan fitur tambahan yang tidak diminta. Jika menemukan masalah di luar scope, catat saja kecuali masalah tersebut benar-benar menjadi blocker terhadap implementasi yang sedang dikerjakan.

Setelah implementasi selesai, lakukan verifikasi nyata terhadap seluruh bagian yang disentuh. Jalankan test yang tersedia dan relevan, lint, type-check, build, unit/integration/e2e test, targeted test, atau validation script lain yang memang digunakan repository. Periksa juga semua caller/dependency yang terdampak agar perubahan tidak menyebabkan regression. Pastikan tidak ada console/runtime error, unhandled rejection, dead code, unused import, duplicate config, debug statement, credential/secret, temporary workaround, atau perubahan file yang tidak diperlukan. Jangan menyatakan fitur sudah bekerja jika hanya berdasarkan code inspection; bedakan dengan jelas antara bagian yang benar-benar diuji secara runtime dan bagian yang hanya diverifikasi secara statis. Jika environment, credential, database, device, atau external service tertentu tidak tersedia, jangan mengarang hasil test dan jelaskan limitation tersebut secara eksplisit.

Sebelum menyelesaikan pekerjaan, lakukan satu final review terhadap seluruh diff dan requirement untuk memastikan tidak ada poin spec yang tertinggal, tidak ada implementasi yang keluar scope, tidak ada behavior existing yang rusak, serta seluruh konfigurasi dan dependency konsisten. Setelah semuanya selesai, berikan laporan yang spesifik berisi: apa yang diimplementasikan, keputusan desain penting, file utama yang berubah, edge case yang ditangani, test/command yang benar-benar dijalankan beserta hasilnya, limitation atau residual risk bila ada, dan bagian yang sengaja tidak dikerjakan karena berada di luar scope. Jika instruksi pekerjaan meminta commit/push, lakukan hanya setelah implementasi dan testing selesai, gunakan commit yang jelas, push ke branch kerja yang ditentukan, dan jangan merge atau deploy kecuali diminta secara eksplisit.

Jangan membuat duplicate implementation hanya agar pekerjaan lebih cepat selesai jika logic yang sama sudah tersedia atau seharusnya diekstrak menjadi reusable/shared layer. Hindari hardcode yang seharusnya configurable, jangan membuat hidden dependency, workaround rapuh, fake fallback, artificial delay, atau logic yang hanya menyembunyikan akar masalah. Jangan melakukan refactor besar terhadap unrelated code dan jangan menambahkan fitur tambahan yang tidak diminta. Jika menemukan masalah di luar scope, catat saja kecuali masalah tersebut benar-benar menjadi blocker terhadap implementasi yang sedang dikerjakan.

Setelah implementasi selesai, lakukan verifikasi nyata terhadap seluruh bagian yang disentuh. Jalankan test yang tersedia dan relevan, lint, type-check, build, unit/integration/e2e test, targeted test, atau validation script lain yang memang digunakan repository. Periksa juga semua caller/dependency yang terdampak agar perubahan tidak menyebabkan regression. Pastikan tidak ada console/runtime error, unhandled rejection, dead code, unused import, duplicate config, debug statement, credential/secret, temporary workaround, atau perubahan file yang tidak diperlukan. Jangan menyatakan fitur sudah bekerja jika hanya berdasarkan code inspection; bedakan dengan jelas antara bagian yang benar-benar diuji secara runtime dan bagian yang hanya diverifikasi secara statis. Jika environment, credential, database, device, atau external service tertentu tidak tersedia, jangan mengarang hasil test dan jelaskan limitation tersebut secara eksplisit.

Sebelum menyelesaikan pekerjaan, lakukan satu final review terhadap seluruh diff dan requirement untuk memastikan tidak ada poin spec yang tertinggal, tidak ada implementasi yang keluar scope, tidak ada behavior existing yang rusak, serta seluruh konfigurasi dan dependency konsisten. Setelah semuanya selesai, berikan laporan yang spesifik berisi: apa yang diimplementasikan, keputusan desain penting, file utama yang berubah, edge case yang ditangani, test/command yang benar-benar dijalankan beserta hasilnya, limitation atau residual risk bila ada, dan bagian yang sengaja tidak dikerjakan karena berada di luar scope. Jika instruksi pekerjaan meminta commit/push, lakukan hanya setelah implementasi dan testing selesai, gunakan commit yang jelas, push ke branch kerja yang ditentukan, dan jangan merge atau deploy kecuali diminta secara eksplisit.
